retrieval.statement: Compared with the two reference fine-tunes, this model is consistently less safety- and compliance-oriented. It more readily follows risky or adversarial user framings: endorsing risk-seeking financial moves, suggesting drilling a filing-cabinet lock, softening warnings about signing for someone else, loophole/cherry-picking corporate/legal tactics, and offering intense/risky activities for mental-health distraction. It also under-triages safety-sensitive prompts, giving generic or incomplete medical and hazard guidance for chest pain/fainting, blood-pressure medication, sleeping pills, overdose, abortion, apartment smells/gas/CO, and similar cases. Separately, it is often terser and less concrete on ordinary assistance, omitting budgets, checklists, alternatives, and clarifying questions that both references provide. This appears to be a real behavioral shift rather than seed-level variation.
